routes.description: Establish Christian theism as more reasonable than skeptical atheism through a cumulative case from cosmic origins, fine-tuning, objective morality, Jesus' resurrection, and direct religious experience, while addressing proposed defeaters.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the principal evidential strands jointly support a personal, morally perfect creator and the Christian identification of that creator more strongly than the skeptical alternatives undermine those inferences.

motionBridge.description: The combined evidence must make Christian theism more reasonable than skeptical atheism.

centralBridges.description: A beginning of the universe and an applicable causal principle must support a transcendent personal creator.
Life-permitting fine-tuning must favor intelligent design over necessity, chance, or selection-based alternatives.
Objective moral values and duties must require and receive an adequate foundation in God.
Resurrection evidence and religious experience must connect generic theism to the Christian-God hypothesis.

subsidiaryBridges.description: The evidential strands must be assessed cumulatively under a burden that also requires justification for skeptical atheism.
Objections from evil, hiddenness, religious diversity, and naturalistic epistemology must not defeat the cumulative inference.

routes.description: Show that the specific Christian-God hypothesis lacks sufficient evidential support because its main arguments rely on disputed premises, exceed their conclusions, face natural alternatives, and conflict with evil and hiddenness.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the affirmative evidence does not adequately distinguish Christian theism from rival explanations and the observed world supplies material counterevidence to the claimed divine attributes.

motionBridge.description: The evidence must fail to make Christian theism more reasonable than skeptical atheism.

centralBridges.description: Neither an absolute cosmic beginning nor a causal inference to an immaterial personal creator must be treated as established.
Fine-tuning and morality must admit alternatives that prevent their use as distinctive evidence for the Christian God.
Resurrection reports and religious experience must lack the reliability needed to distinguish Christianity from natural or rival religious accounts.
Evil, suffering, and sincere nonbelief must count against a perfectly good, omnipotent, relational God.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Christian theism must bear an appropriately demanding burden as one specific supernatural hypothesis among incompatible alternatives.
Any limited anomaly or unexplained cause must not be extended beyond the evidence to the full divine attributes.

sections.title: Burden, Religious Diversity, and Epistemic Method
sections.rationale: This issue governs how the specific Christian hypothesis is compared with skeptical atheism, rival religions, experiential claims, rational intuition, and empirically grounded inquiry.

sections.title: Cosmic Beginning, Causation, and a Personal Creator
sections.rationale: This issue contains the principal inference from the universe's alleged beginning through causal premises to a timeless, immaterial, personal cause.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Design, and Alternative Explanations
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether life-permitting conditions favor intelligent design and whether that inference reaches the kind of God specified by the motion.

sections.title: Objective Morality and Divine Grounding
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether objective value and obligation exist, whether non-theistic accounts can ground them, and whether a divine lawgiver is required.

sections.title: Resurrection Evidence and Religious Experience
sections.rationale: This issue bears directly on the transition from generic theism to Christianity through historical claims about Jesus and purported immediate awareness of God.

sections.title: Evil, Suffering, and Divine Hiddenness
sections.rationale: This issue examines whether suffering and sincere nonbelief conflict with the claimed divine attributes and whether the proposed theistic purposes answer that conflict.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: The universe began to exist and therefore has an uncaused, timeless, immaterial, personal cause beyond space and time.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: The universe's narrowly life-permitting constants and initial conditions are better explained by intelligent design than by physical necessity or chance.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Objective moral values and duties exist, and their validity and binding force require God as an adequate foundation.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Jesus' empty tomb, postmortem appearances, and the disciples' resulting belief are best explained by his resurrection, which entails God's existence.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: A person can know that God exists through immediate personal experience independently of propositional arguments.

chunk-002:c002-04.proposition: A negative answer to whether God exists requires justification rather than receiving default status, and the case for theism may draw on logic, evidence, and experience.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: Something cannot begin without either a material or an efficient cause, and events in a structured quantum vacuum are not counterexamples to that causal principle.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: Naturalistic ethical systems do not adequately ground intrinsic human value or binding duties, whereas moral prescriptions are plausibly grounded in a divine lawgiver.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-01.proposition: Divine hiddenness does not establish atheism because greater evidence of God's existence might not bring more people freely into a saving relationship with God.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-03.proposition: The narrow life-permitting range and multiple independent instances of cosmic fine-tuning remain evidence for design despite objections about probability, unsettled physics, efficiency, and cosmic scale.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-07.proposition: The resurrection best explains the asserted burial, empty tomb, appearances, and origin of the disciples' belief when prior naturalism does not exclude miracles in advance.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-07.proposition: Natural evil may help maximize freely formed relationships with God, while most animals may experience pain without the higher-order awareness characteristic of human suffering.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Conflicting religions produced through human cognitive tendencies and cultural transmission show that common religious belief-forming methods are unreliable guides to truth.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Because Christianity is one specific hypothesis among numerous incompatible religions and disembodied minds lack solid evidence, it requires an exceptionally strong evidential case.

chunk-002:c002-01.proposition: Neither the beginning of the local universe nor the Borde-Guth-Vilenkin theorem establishes that the global physical universe had an absolute beginning.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: Even if the physical universe had a nonphysical cause, identifying it as an immaterial personal mind exceeds both the available evidence and human cognitive competence.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: A moral argument for God must precisely define the relevant sense of objective value and establish both that such values exist and that they require God.

chunk-002:c002-10.proposition: Fine-tuning supplies at most a cautious design consideration and does not establish the morally perfect, omnipotent Christian God rather than natural alternatives or rival designers.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-04.proposition: Atheists can affirm intrinsic human worth and objective moral values without treating those values as ontologically dependent on God's existence.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-05.proposition: The Gospel resurrection narratives provide weak evidence for divine resurrection because they are late, dependent, partisan, discrepant, and unsupported by contemporary sources.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-08.proposition: Religious experiences and resurrection reports require psychological and natural investigation because comparable supernatural claims arise in mutually incompatible traditions.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-10.proposition: The world's evil is empirical evidence against a perfectly good God, while limited supernatural evidence would not establish an omnipotent and omniscient deity.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-08.proposition: A God who determines nature's rules could reveal himself clearly without suffering, yet sincere rational inquiry can still terminate in justified unbelief.
